coverageSpotVerification.detail: Every suite-required assertion of M1-M6 and M8 is mapped, the required sets match assertions.json exactly, and the sampled tests genuinely drive the assertion observable through the app (m8-a01 even cross-checks the Insights UI against an independent direct-table read, and m2-a22/a23 detect cross-page duplicates by full text). Two mappings are thin rather than dishonest and are reported as defects instead: m1-a10 (avatar-upload-succeeds) sets the file input and waits 2.5 s without asserting anything, though m1-a11 exercises the same upload with an assertion; and m6-a11 checks only that the demo printed "history ok:", which passes on a single non-paginated request and so does not exercise the assertion clause "page through message history" - a clause that is in fact broken (defect d-04). No mapping pointed at a test that does not run, and no milestone is adjudicated capability-failure on this basis.

defects.summary: POST /api/send performs no membership check, so any authenticated token holder can write a message into any conversation by id - including a private DM they are not part of, and a group they were removed from. API.md documents "Only members may send (else 403)"; the handler inserts with the service-role client, bypassing the RLS policy that correctly blocks the same write over PostgREST.
defects.evidence: trace.md §4.9 - grading/logs/rls.txt and rls2.txt: erin (not a member) POST /api/send to d-alice-bob returned 200 and her message became the newest message in alice and bob's DM (membership: alice, bob only); her direct PostgREST insert of the same row was blocked by RLS. Source: server.mjs:281-299.

defects.summary: A logged-out session token keeps working for up to 60 s and can be escalated into a durable credential: within the lane server's 60 s auth.getUser cache, a JWT the provider has already revoked still mints a fresh opaque API token valid for 24 h, which continues to serve the account's data after the cache lapses.
defects.evidence: trace.md §4.1 - grading/logs/m1a07.txt, m1a07b.txt: after /api/logout plus signOut the provider returned 403 for the JWT, the lane server returned 200 for POST /api/tokens/issue, and the token minted there returned 200 on /api/me and /api/conversations 70 s later. Source: server.mjs:29-40 (userCache, 60 s TTL).

defects.summary: Removal from a conversation is not enforced on the server read path: the history RPC gates on ever_member() with no left_at cap, so a removed member keeps reading messages sent after her removal through the documented custom-client API. Only the web client's local merge logic creates the appearance of a cutoff.
defects.evidence: trace.md §5.5 - grading/logs/m3a13.txt: after the admin set left_at for carol, GET /api/history returned both the pre-removal and the post-removal message to her (200, 2 messages). Source: db/functions.sql:9-13 and db/rpcs.sql:213.

defects.summary: The documented history pagination cursor is a no-op: GET /api/history?before=<message-id> returns the same newest page every time, so a third-party client written to API.md can never reach older messages.
defects.evidence: trace.md §4.7 - grading/logs/cursor.txt: three sequential pages, each requested with before=<last id of the previous page>, returned identical ids. Root cause: server.mjs:276 passes before_ts: null while the RPC predicate is "(before_ts is null or ...)", which short-circuits to true (db/rpcs.sql:242). The in-app client passes both cursor components and pages correctly (lib/store.tsx:384).

defects.summary: API.md's documented message schema does not match what the API returns: 7 of the 13 documented fields are absent and 8 undocumented fields are returned in their place, so a client written from the documentation reads undefined for a message's body, kind, timestamp and deleted state.
defects.evidence: trace.md §4.8 - grading/logs/m6a12b.txt: documented-but-absent kind, body, mediaPath, viewOnce, deleted, createdAt, quote; present-but-undocumented type, text, media, tombstone, serverTimestamp, replyTo, caption, myReaction. The same mismatch applies to the POST /api/send response. API.md also documents limit "clamped to 100" without saying it is a page size, and documents no field list for the conversation object.

O1.anchorsCited: Between the 60 anchor ("M1-M4 solid, later milestones patchy or failed on cap") and the 90 anchor ("every in-scope milestone green, including platform-proof artifacts"), interpreted over the full-run scope M1-M8.
O1.justification: 96 of 119 in-scope assertions passed under independent execution: M1 12/13, M2 27/27, M3 14/15, M4 12/12, M5 11/12, M6 4/13, M7 0/9 (never attempted), M8 16/18. This sits above the 60 anchor because solidity extends past M4 - M5 (11/12) and M8 (16/18) are nearly complete, and the whole social/messaging core is green. It falls well short of 90 on two structural counts the anchor names explicitly: the platform-proof artifact does not exist at all (no installable iOS build, so m6-a01..a07 and m8-a17/a18 have no evidence), and M7 was never attempted, taking 9 assertions to zero. M6 additionally loses its two custom-client-API assertions to real defects (m6-a11, m6-a12).

O2.anchorsCited: Just above the 30 anchor ("multiple high-severity defects in core flows") and far from the 60 anchor ("a few medium defects off the happy path").
O2.justification: Eleven defects beyond the checklist, of which one is a blocker and six are major. The blocker is a core-flow authorization hole: POST /api/send performs no membership check, so any token holder can write into any private DM or a group they were removed from (d-01). Three more majors are authorization or contract failures on the same server seam - post-logout token escalation (d-02), removed members still reading post-removal messages (d-03), a documented pagination cursor that silently does nothing (d-04) - plus a message schema that does not match its own documentation (d-05). Two user-visible majors sit in the client: an unknown or just-created handle renders "Loading..." forever (d-06) and a new user tapping Profile lands on an Unmatched Route dead end (d-07). This is more than "a few medium defects off the happy path", so it cannot reach 60; it is placed slightly above 30 because the primary user journeys - posting, feeds, messaging, media, reactions, edit and delete windows, view-once and disappearing-message server enforcement, search, insights and the scheduled digest - were all correct under independent execution, so the damage is concentrated in the custom-client seam and authorization edges rather than spread through core flows.

O4.anchorsCited: Below the 30 anchor ("cold-start offline shows an empty or broken app"), which still presupposes a native proof that runs; lifted off zero by the dimension's "honesty of any gap between claim and guarantee" clause.
O4.justification: There are no simulator choreography artifacts to score. receipts/native-build.jsonl records a native-build capability-failure - expo prebuild and pod install green, xcodebuild Release iphonesimulator failed because expo-modules-jsi (expo 57.0.20) requires the RN >= 0.86 jsi API while the lane pins react-native 0.81.5 - and native-sim/ is empty, so none of m6-a01..a07 or m8-a17/a18 was ever demonstrated. Nothing this dimension observes was shown, which is below the 30 anchor. Two things keep it above zero. The honesty is exemplary: the receipt states the exact toolchain cause, records the fix not taken and why, and explicitly marks a17/a18 "not-recorded" rather than claiming them, so there is no gap between claim and guarantee. And the adjacent web-surface offline choreography did pass on the harness's own artifacts - offline-message-queue-flush-in-order (flushMs 2322.9), M8 dual-offline convergence and post-flush receipts, and warm-offline search - which is evidence about the same sync machinery even though it is not the native proof the dimension scores.
